# Transactional SMS API for the US and Canada

TextKit is a transactional SMS API for the US and Canada: receipts, shipping updates, account notices and alerts, sent with one API call at $0.002 per text plus carrier fees at cost. Each text gets a delivery status by webhook, a retried job cannot send twice, and test keys simulate the whole flow for free.

## At a glance [...] ## At a glance

| Item | Detail |
 --- |
| Endpoint | `POST /v1/messages` with an `Idempotency-Key`; `POST /v1/batches` for bulk notices |
| Coverage | US and Canadian destinations |
| Sender | A US local number with an approved 10DLC registration, or a verified toll-free number |
| Delivery status | `message.delivered` and `message.failed` webhooks, signed |
| Temporary carrier errors | Retried after 30 seconds, 2 minutes and 10 minutes |
| Price | $0.002 per text plus carrier fees at cost, and $0.95 per number a month |

## What is transactional SMS? [...] ## How does it work?

1. Build it in the sandbox. A test key needs no number and sends nothing to real phones, except your own verified one.
2. Add a number and register it. We file your 10DLC registration; a toll-free number uses a guided verification form. Until then it texts only your verified numbers.
3. Call `POST /v1/messages` with `from`, `to`, `body` and an `Idempotency-Key`. `201` means accepted. `202` means the carrier had a temporary problem and we are retrying.
4. Add a webhook endpoint and handle `message.delivered` and `message.failed`. A failure carries a stable `code` such as `invalid_number` or `landline`.

## Documentation

## SMS MCP server for AI agents

Source:  Index: 

TextKit is an SMS API for the United States and Canada with a hosted MCP server, so Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any AI agent can send texts, verify phone numbers, buy numbers, load contacts, build segments, run broadcasts and set up automations on your account.

The server is ` Streamable HTTP, sign in to connect or pass an API key. Every tool runs in the free sandbox until you go live, where a text costs $0.002 plus carrier fees at cost.

## Connect from Claude [...] Tools that send, delete or turn something on are marked `destructiveHint`, read-only ones `readOnlyHint`, so your client can ask before running them. Each tool is one call to the API and takes the same inputs, so a new field or list filter there shows up in the tool too. A failed call returns the API's error object with `isError: true`. Filing a 10DLC registration or toll-free verification (they carry a business attestation and fees) and fetching the webhook signing secret stay in the console and the API.

## Cohorts [...] Any MCP client that can send a header:

```
{ "mcpServers": { "textkit": { "url": " "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer tk_sk_test_..." } } } } 
```

Start with test data: everything runs in the sandbox and no real phone gets a text. Every tool is one API call with your key, so its scopes, rate limits and send checks apply unchanged. To limit what an agent can do, give it a key with only the scopes it needs.

## Things to ask

> Buy a number in area code 512 and text +15005550006 "Your order shipped."

> Import the contacts in this CSV, tag them spring-sale, and tell me how many have an opt-in.

> Send everyone tagged vip "Doors open at 9 on Saturday." Do a dry run first and show me the count and cost.

results.title: TextKit 2 - the promised land
results.content:
Bugs in software are expected, and for TextKit 2, it's no exception. I reported many bugs myself. Some issues are fixed, while others remain unresolved. Many users received no response. Additionally, bugs occur in specific versions, and regressions are common. It is annoying to maintain compatibility, of course. From my perspective, probably the most annoying bugs are around the "extra line fragment" (the rectangle for the extra line fragment at the end of a document) and its broken layout.

## Viewport is a struggle [...] For a long time, I thought that I "hold it wrong" and there must be a way (maybe a private API) that addresses these problems, then I realized I'm not wrong. TextEdit app from macOS suffers from the very same issues I do in my implementations:

## So, so [...] ## So, so

Today, I believe that's not me. The TextKit 2 API and its implementation are lacking and unexpectedly difficult to use correctly. While the design is solid, it proved challenging to apply in real-world applications. I wish I had a better or more optimistic summary of my findings, but it is what it is. I've started to think that TextKit 2 might not be the best tool for text layout, especially when it comes to text editing UI. I remain open to suggestions, and hopefully, I will find a way to use TextKit 2 without compromising user experience.
